title: Density average of a multiplicative derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\psi$ be a probability density on $(\\mathbb F_2)^n$, and let $F:(\\mathbb F_2)^n\\to\\mathbb R$. Define the multiplicative derivative in direction $y$ by $D_yF(x)=F(x+y)F(x)$. Then the uniform average over $y$ of the $\\psi$-weighted average of $D_yF$ equals $(\\mathbb E_xF(x))\\,\\mathbb E_{x\\sim\\psi}F(x)$, where $\\mathbb E_{x\\sim\\psi}F(x)=\\mathbb E_x\\psi(x)F(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $\\psi$ is a pointwise nonnegative function on $(\\mathbb F_2)^n$ with uniform average $1$
